failure_summary.description: Search or refinement results were not assigned to local variables and saved under new cache keys.
The newly provided restaurant neighborhood was omitted from the filter call.
Flight time bounds were converted to an invalid format and did not represent the requested exact departure and latest-arrival limits.
Hotel dates were invented instead of requested, and the independently actionable restaurant search was skipped.

patch.reasoning: Clarify the tool-call lifecycle in a way that directly rules out bare calls, and make cache refinement require the new criterion rather than a no-op filter. Add explicit semantics and formatting for time-range requests. The missing-date trajectory already conflicts with the existing prohibition on inventing mandatory values, so avoid repeating the previously rejected missing-information edit.

edits.target: - Bind the exact return value of every search, filter, sort, and nearest-results call to a variable, then save it with `save_to_cache` under a unique, descriptive key. Save refined results under a new key. Do not substitute hand-built dictionaries or redefined models for tool result objects.
edits.content: - For every search, filter, sort, and nearest-results call, assign the exact return value to a local variable and then call `save_to_cache` with that variable under a unique, descriptive key; use a new key for refinements. Never leave one of these planning calls as a bare expression or nest it only as another call’s argument. Do not substitute hand-built dictionaries or redefined models for tool result objects.

edits.target: - When refining a cached result, do not resend criteria already represented in that result; apply the newly introduced preference with the appropriate filter.
edits.content: - When refining a cached result, pass it as `prior_results` and include every newly introduced, schema-supported criterion in the filter call; do not resend criteria already represented in the result. A call that passes only `prior_results` is not a refinement.

edits.target: ## Validate tool arguments and preserve user intent
edits.content: - For flight time ranges, use the time format accepted by the tool (for example, `08:23 PM`), not 24-hour strings with seconds. An exact time (“at 8:23 PM”) uses that time for both range endpoints; “by” or “no later than” a time uses the start of the day through that time, and “after” or “no earlier than” uses that time through the end of the day.
